entry.summary: Up to 90 days without a visa.
entry.max_stay: 90 days, with one paid extension of up to 90 more
entry.other: Overstaying can bring fines and a ban.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The US Dollar is the legal currency of Ecuador. It's useful to have $US1 notes. Many smaller shops and taxi drivers don't change large notes. ATMs are available around the country. Credit cards are accepted in hotels, restaurants and tourist facilities in major centres. Contact your bank to check that your card will work.

consular.mission: Australian Consulate, Guayaquil; Canadian Embassy, Quito; Australian Embassy, Santiago de Chile
consular.notes: There's an Australian Consulate in Guayaquil, Ecuador. It can provide limited consular help. The Canadian Embassy in Quito, Ecuador gives consular assistance to Australians in Ecuador under the Canada-Australia Consular Services Sharing Agreement. For issue of provisional travel documents, contact the: - Australian Consulate in Guayaquil - Canadian Embassy in Quito

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and include long prison terms in local jails. Minimum sentence for trafficking or consuming 'soft drugs', such as marijuana (cannabis), can be 1 to 2 years in jail. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: You must always carry photo identification in Ecuador. Authorities may detain you if you don't.
laws.heading: Proof of identity

laws.rule: Political activity by foreigners is illegal. This includes joining protests or demonstrations. If you participate, authorities may detain or deport you.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: For the first six months after you arrive in Ecuador you can drive with both: a valid Australian driver's licence an International Driving Permit (IDP) You must get your IDP before departing Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

health-entry.notes: You'll need to show proof of vaccination against yellow fever if you have spent more than 10 days in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia or Peru before entering Ecuador. Check di. Australia asks for a yellow fever certificate when you return from a country with yellow fever risk.

items.text: Travellers have been robbed and sexually assaulted after accepting 'spiked' drinks and food, as well as chewing gum and cigarettes.
